chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali, from Abd Allah ibn al-Salt, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

When you draw out the deceased, then say: In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and upon the creed of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. O Allah, toward Your mercy and not toward Your punishment.
And when you place him in the lahd, then place your mouth upon his ears and say: Allah is your Lord, Islam is your religion, Muhammad is your Prophet, the Quran is your Book, and Ali is your Imam.

key_terms.إِمَامُكَ: your Imam, affirming rightful religious authority
key_terms.اللَّحْدِ: the burial niche in the grave
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامُ: the religion affirmed for the deceased
key_terms.الْقُرْآنُ: the divine Book professed in the burial talqin
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person being prepared for burial
key_terms.رَحْمَتِكَ: Your mercy, sought for the deceased at burial
key_terms.عَذَابِكَ: Your punishment, from which protection is sought
key_terms.مِلَّةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the creed and religious way of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What should be recited when placing a deceased person into the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the prescribed words to be recited when handling and burying the deceased. It combines supplication for divine mercy with a talqin affirming the deceased's creed, including belief in Allah, Islam, the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the Quran, and the Imamate of Ali عليه السلام.
